stories.title: Bank of America fined $1.2 bn for money‑laundering reporting failures
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department announced on Tuesday that Bank of America will pay a $1.2 bn (£910 m) civil penalty for not reporting over $5 bn in suspicious transactions, including about $1 bn that posed national‑security and illicit‑finance risks. The Treasury said the bank failed to flag activity possibly linked to Chinese money‑laundering networks and trade‑based schemes with a substantial nexus to the U.S. southwest border. The announcement came less than 24 hours before the bank’s scheduled earnings release.
stories.why: The penalty underscores heightened regulatory scrutiny of major banks’ anti‑money‑laundering controls ahead of a key earnings report.

stories.title: India and US trade talks near completion, says External Affairs Minister
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said that negotiations on a trade deal between India and the United States are moving toward a “landing point.” Both sides are working to resolve remaining issues, and officials are engaged in intensive discussions. Jaishankar noted the talks are complex because the US is simultaneously finalising competitive agreements with other economies and highlighted the role of tariffs in the US re‑industrialisation agenda.
stories.why: The outcome could reshape tariff structures and market access for businesses in both countries.

stories.title: Character.AI files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and plans asset sale to Disney
stories.summary: Character.AI, an interactive chatbot platform that lets users create AI characters, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy five years after its launch, reporting assets and liabilities between $50 million and $100 million. The company agreed to sell selected assets to Disney for $20 million and grant a non‑exclusive perpetual license, with Disney providing transition services through former Character.AI staff. The sale process is expected to close in late November or early December, and no full‑company buyer has emerged.
stories.why: The filing could reshape the consumer AI chatbot market and marks Disney’s entry into AI character technology.

stories.title: Bonus issue, stock split and dividend alert! Last day to buy these 3 stocks before record date. Do you own any?
stories.summary: Around three companies have fixed October 15 as the record date for their respective corporate actions including bonus issue, stock split and dividend, effectively making today the last day for interested investors to buy shares of the company to be eligible for the rewards. Oneclick Logistics India has fixed Thursday as the record date for its 1:2 bonus issue.
stories.why: This can affect market expectations, company valuations, sector sentiment or capital flows.

stories.title: IMF warns of risks from AI boom and debt, but raises forecast for world growth
stories.summary: The international body slightly upgraded its outlook for the world economy, but warned that risks of an AI-related market correction and job losses because of the technology, as well as government debt, remain concerns. That's up from its July forecast for three per cent growth and well below the 3.5 per cent expansion in 2025.
stories.why: This matters because it could affect economic conditions, trade, technology, public systems or international decisions.

stories.title: RBI Governor says more steps may be taken to curb FX speculation
stories.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the Reserve Bank of India may consider additional measures to curb speculative foreign‑exchange trading and keep the currency market orderly. He noted that recent restrictions are meant to support genuine hedging needs, not to impose broad capital controls.
stories.why: The stance could influence currency volatility and hedging costs for Indian businesses and investors.

stories.title: Science Corp implants vision‑restoring PRIMA chip in first Stargardt disease patient
stories.summary: Science Corporation announced that its PRIMA retinal implant was surgically placed in a patient with Stargardt disease, marking the first use of the device for this inherited condition. CEO Max Hodak disclosed the procedure on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt, noting that PRIMA is already commercially available in Europe for geographic atrophy and could be adapted for other retinal disorders. Stargardt disease affects roughly 150,000 people worldwide and leads to progressive central vision loss.
stories.why: The implantation demonstrates a potential therapeutic option for a currently incurable disease that impacts many patients.

stories.title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
stories.summary: Cerebras Systems CEO and co-founder Andrew Feldman thinks the AI doomer narrative isn’t doing the industry any favors. He thinks AI leaders should spend more time telling people that AI could lead to a world where your grandkids will “never meet anybody who dies of cancer,” for instance, even if they have concerns about AI risks.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.
